```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The question asks for a paying customer within 90 days. A has the shorter path. Its brief describes a thin Whisper-API wrapper with no regulatory gate. B's own brief says COPPA consent, a privacy notice and a legal consult must be done before any launch, and that child-product trust 'typically builds over months.' Both eat directly into the 90-day window.",
    "A's demand evidence is direct and sourced. Two independent Reddit threads (r/automation, r/selfpublish) and an HN thread state the exact price complaint. The forums where the complaint appears are also the proposed zero-cost acquisition channel, so demand and distribution overlap.",
    "A's crowding is real, but it also signals that people pay. Lessrec, Speechnotes and TranscribeBee all charge per minute with no subscription, which validates willingness to pay at the proposed price. The goal is one paying customer, not category leadership.",
    "B's pricing is squeezed between a free, well-resourced incumbent (Khan Academy Kids) and a $500/month outlier that drew public backlash. B also faces efficacy scrutiny in parent communities that an unproven solo curriculum is poorly placed to survive quickly.",
    "B's acquisition evidence is weaker. Its organic-channel cost is marked [unsourced], and it supplies no evidence that parents convert from community posts. A's organic channel is similarly unproven on conversion, but it carries no trust or regulatory barrier."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's lead demand quote, 'Ultimately, I decided not to pay $500 a month for the Mentava app for my daughter,' is evidence of a parent declining to pay. It does not show demand for B's offering. The supporting claim that parents pay tutors $25–$120/hour cites only 'multiple tutoring-cost sources' with no URL, so it counts as unsourced.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. A wins on speed to a first payment, not on business quality. Its brief openly describes a commoditizing market with a low price ceiling, and several of its downside claims (Google's free on-device app, Untold bundling transcription free) carry no URLs. If the question were long-term viability or revenue per customer, B's higher proven price point would weigh more. Under the 90-day first-customer criterion, B's regulatory and trust friction is the deciding factor."
}
```
